subject: Clarifying streaming guarantees and proposed amendment for POC
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@symmetryhealth.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@symmetryhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify streaming guarantees for POC - Symmetry

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're lining up a 6-week POC and need to lock down the service guarantees so our procurement and SRE teams can sign off. A few concrete asks:

- For streaming endpoints (server-sent tokens), what is Redwood's Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) commitment? We need both typical and worst-case (p50 / p95) numbers for hosted vs dedicated deployments.
- What sustained token/sec expectations do you guarantee under the Dedicated plan (tokens/sec per replica and cluster-level)?
- If streaming falls back to a buffered (non-streaming) mode due to load or degradation, how is that detected and how quickly will the fallback occur? We need an explicit detection window and the behavioral SLA (e.g., timeframe to notify + mitigation).
- How do these behaviors map to uptime credits or cost adjustments? Procurement needs a simple matrix.

Would appreciate a short note or a one-pager we can attach to the SOW. If easier, loop in your legal/ops folks and we can do a quick call this week.

Alex
Technical Program Manager
Symmetry Health

--

Subject: Re: Clarify streaming guarantees for POC - Symmetry

Hi Alex — great to hear the POC is moving forward. I captured a concise response below and attached a two-sheet matrix (SLA_Diff_Matrix.xlsx) that maps guarantees to credit tiers. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through.

Summary (high-level):
- Hosted API (standard): TTFT target p50 = 150ms; p95 = 550ms.
- Dedicated (reserved): TTFT target p50 = 120ms; p95 = 400ms.
- Sustained token/sec: Dedicated guarantees are expressed per reserved replica: baseline 60 tokens/sec/replica sustained under expected seq profiles; cluster autoscaling behavior is documented in the matrix.
- Fallback behavior: Streaming fallback (to buffered delivery) is triggered after 2 consecutive token backpressure detections over a 3s window or when the endpoint enters degraded node-level health. Notification to the customer will be via the Console incident channel and an in-band header on responses. Fallback window for mitigation is immediate; permanent fallback persists until autoscaler restores capacity.
- Credits: For sustained degradation affecting >5% of requests in an hour we propose a sliding credit scale (see matrix). Short transient fallbacks (<5 minutes) are operational incidents and not credit-eligible unless repeated.

I'll attach the matrix and a draft amendment we can propose to procurement. Jordan/Markus — flagging for legal and SRE confirmation on the fallback detection thresholds and credit language.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Forwarding Alex's note with internal comments.

On Mon, 10 Jun 2029 at 12:08, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Alex — great to hear the POC is moving forward. I captured a concise response below...

Internal notes / proposed tweaks:
- TTFT numbers above look reasonable for hosted/dedicated POCs, but legal will ask for concrete measurement definitions. Suggest we phrase TTFT as "time from request completion to first non-empty token in the HTTP stream, measured at the customer's egress region using synthetic probes" and include a test harness clause.
- Fallback detection: 2 consecutive token backpressure in 3s window is fine for detection. We should add a 30s cooldown to avoid flip-flopping on noisy networks. Also define a maximum staged fallback of 10 minutes before automatic re-evaluation; beyond that, escalate to ops and notify the customer with remediation ETA.
- Credits: instead of sliding credits starting at 5%, propose a tiered approach:
  * Tier A: >20% degraded for 1 hour = 10% monthly credit on affected endpoints.
  * Tier B: 5%–20% degraded for 1 hour = 5% credit.
  * Transient <5% or <5 minutes: operational noise, no credit.

Ask Markus to confirm whether 60 tokens/sec/replica sustained is realistic across quantized model variants and whether we should include a note about model family variance (larger models reduce tokens/sec).

-jordan

Subject: Proposed amendment: streaming emission guarantees and fallback policy (POC)

Alex / Symmetry legal —

Thanks for the patience while we aligned internally. Attached is a short amendment (redwood_draft_amendment.pdf) and the SLA matrix. Below is a plain-English summary of the commitments we are willing to include for the POC SOW. If that looks good I can circulate a DocuSign for both the SOW and the amendment.

Summary of proposed POC commitments:
- Measurement definition: TTFT is measured at the customer egress region from request completion to first non-empty token delivered over the streaming response. Measurements use Redwood synthetic probes (we'll share the harness details).
- TTFT targets (p50 / p95): Hosted: 150ms / 550ms. Dedicated: 120ms / 400ms.
- Sustained throughput guarantee (Dedicated only): baseline 60 tokens/sec per reserved replica; note in amendment that model family and sequence length materially affect tokens/sec and that we will list applicable model families for the POC.
- Fallback detection and behavior: Streaming fallback will be initiated after 2 consecutive token emission failures within a 3s sliding window, with a 30s cooldown to prevent oscillation. Automatic restoration will attempt periodically; if fallback persists longer than 10 minutes we will notify the customer and provide remediation ETA.
- Credits: Tiered credit approach for sustained degradation affecting successful streaming delivery:
  * >20% of requests degraded for 1 hour: 10% credit on monthly charges for affected endpoints.
  * 5%–20% degraded for 1 hour: 5% credit.
  * Transient short incidents (<5 minutes or <5% of requests): operational incidents, no credit.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm acceptance of the measurement definition and the 10-minute persistent fallback window.
2) If accepted, I'll send DocuSign links for the amendment + SOW and propose a 2-week canary starting the week of 24 Jun.

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk legal and SRE through the definitions.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
